page: Amazon Web Services c6id.12xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the x86_64 architecture. It features 48 vCPUs derived from 24 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8375C processor operating at a clock speed of 3.5 GHz. The instance is configured with 96.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, which provides a memory-to-vCPU ratio of 2.0 GB per core. Local storage is bundled directly with the instance, offering 2850 GB of NVMe SSD capacity, while network connectivity is supported by a baseline bandwidth of 19 Gbps managed via the Nitro hypervisor.

Benchmark data shows solid performance across multiple compute and cryptographic workloads. The system achieves a Passmark CPU score of 48783.94 and a multi-core Geekbench score of 15844.0. It exhibits strong performance in image processing with a Geekbench score of 15412.0 and in CPU encryption with a Passmark score of 43659.0, both placing in the top 25% tier. For language model workloads, the instance processes prompts at 2456.37 tokens per second and generates text at 306.31 tokens per second using a small 135M model, though performance scales down to 9.01 tokens per second for prompt processing on a large 70B model.

The primary tradeoff of the c6id.12xlarge lies in its memory density. With only 2 GB of RAM per vCPU, it is less suited for memory-bound applications compared to general-purpose or memory-optimized instances. However, the inclusion of 2850 GB of fast local NVMe SSD storage provides high resource density for data-intensive operations. This hardware profile offers qualitative cost efficiency for workloads that demand high compute power and fast local scratch space without requiring massive memory footprints.

This instance is well-suited for compute-heavy and storage-dependent workloads. Appropriate applications include high-performance web serving, software compilation, image processing, and database operations that benefit from direct access to high-speed local NVMe storage. It is also viable for moderate-scale machine learning inference and cryptographic tasks.
